question: Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, when does an EV battery reach the end of its usable life, what can be done with such batteries, and which of those does the review say they all eventually need?

rendered: Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standards, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity is less than 80% of the rated capacity[1]. At that point the end-of-life EV batteries can be reused or repurposed, recycled, or disposed of in landfills, which the review says would cause serious environmental issues. Repurposing reconfigures the batteries for a second life in applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage. Regardless of whether the batteries are reused, the review says they they will eventually need to be[2] recycled[3]. So recycling is the step all of them eventually need.
